page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 6 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AVX512_BF16. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfr7.3xlarge in the average performance tier across most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6723.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 13872.98. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 698.81 GB/sec, which drops to 69.85 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The system demonstrates strong throughput in specific database and web serving tasks, handling 11.99 million Redis SET operations per second and delivering 10.32 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

While the instance is highly capable for memory-intensive workloads, it exhibits clear performance limitations in complex computational tasks. For example, LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are weak, yielding only 17.76 tokens/second for prompt processing and 8.57 tokens/second for text generation. Additionally, the lack of bundled local storage requires reliance on external network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy applications. Given its high memory density and moderate compute profile, this instance is well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, moderate web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring a larger memory footprint without the cost of high-vCPU configurations.
